question: The four-member math team at Pecanridge Middle School is chosen from the math club, which has three girls and five boys. How many different teams made up of two girls and two boys could be chosen?
solution:
Order does not matter within a team. Choose two of the three girls in \(\binom{3}{2}=3\) ways and two of the five boys in \(\binom{5}{2}=5\cdot4/2=10\) ways. Each choice of girls can be paired with every choice of boys, and each pair gives a distinct team, so the count is \(3\cdot10=30\).
Final answer: 30
